components.note: 鱼 (fish) — marks fish and sea creatures, as in 鲜, 鲸 whale, 鳄 crocodile; 鲨 is a shark.
沙 (shā) gives the sound exactly: 鲨 shā.
鱼 (fish) — a picture of a fish: head on top, scaly body 田, tail 一. As a radical (鱼) it marks fish, as in 鲨, 鲜.

example.hanzi: 那片海域经常出现鲨鱼。
example.pinyin: nà piàn hǎiyù jīngcháng chūxiàn shāyú.
example.english: Sharks often appear in that stretch of ocean.
example.fact: Sharks have existed for more than 400 million years, predating dinosaurs by roughly 200 million years, and have survived multiple mass extinction events. Unlike most fish, sharks have no bones at all; their skeletons are made entirely of cartilage, the same flexible tissue found in human ears and noses. This lightweight skeleton, combined with an oil-rich liver instead of a swim bladder, helps them stay buoyant without needing to constantly swim.

examples.hanzi: 水族馆里有一条很大的鲨鱼。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐzúguǎn lǐ yǒu yì tiáo hěn dà de shāyú.
examples.english: There is a very large shark in the aquarium.

examples.hanzi: 我小时候很怕鲨鱼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎo shíhou hěn pà shāyú.
examples.english: I was very afraid of sharks when I was little.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and lips, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 吻 is a kiss.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for wěn; 物 wù shares the part.

example.hanzi: 他们在雨中接吻。
example.pinyin: tāmen zài yǔzhōng jiēwěn.
example.english: They kissed in the rain.
example.fact: The world's longest recorded continuous kiss, set in Thailand in 2013, lasted 58 hours, 35 minutes, and 58 seconds. Kissing triggers a rush of oxytocin and dopamine, the same chemicals linked to bonding and stress relief, which is part of why researchers study it across cultures. Curiously, anthropologists have found that romantic kissing is not universal — some traditional societies show no historical evidence of the practice at all.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的男女主角在最后接吻了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de nánnǚ zhǔjué zài zuìhòu jiēwěn le.
examples.english: In the movie, the lead couple kiss at the end.

examples.hanzi: 公共场所里不要随便接吻。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ lǐ búyào suíbiàn jiēwěn.
examples.english: Don't kiss casually in public places.

components.note: 乘 (chéng) — to ride; as a part it sounds out 剩 shèng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.

example.hanzi: 公交车上有很多乘客。
example.pinyin: gōngjiāochē shàng yǒu hěnduō chéngkè.
example.english: There are many passengers on the bus.
example.fact: The Beijing Subway, which opened in 1969 as China's first metro line, now carries roughly 10 million passenger trips on an average weekday. That makes it one of the busiest rapid-transit systems on Earth, rivaling the combined daily ridership of several major European metro networks.

examples.hanzi: 飞机上的乘客都系好了安全带。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī shàng de chéngkè dōu jì hǎo le ānquándài.
examples.english: The passengers on the plane all fastened their seat belts.

examples.hanzi: 请乘客们从后门下车。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chéngkèmen cóng hòumén xià chē.
examples.english: Passengers, please get off through the back door.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 这条通道通向地下停车场。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo tōngdào tōngxiàng dìxià tíngchēchǎng.
example.english: This passage leads to the underground parking lot.
example.fact: The Panama Canal, completed in 1914 after a decade of construction that cost roughly 25,000 workers' lives to disease and accidents, shortened the sea route between the Atlantic and Pacific by about 8,000 nautical miles. Ships still queue for hours to pass through its lock system today.

examples.hanzi: 火灾时请从安全通道离开。
examples.pinyin: Huǒzāi shí qǐng cóng ānquán tōngdào líkāi.
examples.english: In case of fire, please leave through the emergency exit.

examples.hanzi: 这个通道太窄了，大箱子过不去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tōngdào tài zhǎi le, dà xiāngzi guò bu qù.
examples.english: This passage is too narrow for a big suitcase to get through.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 铁, 银, 钟; early money was metal coins.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 钱 is qián; 戋 also sounds out 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn, and means small or thin.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服的价钱太贵了。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn yīfu de jiàqian tài guì le.
example.english: The price of this piece of clothing is too expensive.
example.fact: Salt was so valuable in the ancient world that Roman soldiers were sometimes partly paid in it — the English word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium,' tied to the Latin word for salt, 'sal.' Scarcity, not just usefulness, has driven the price of ordinary goods throughout history.

examples.hanzi: 你能告诉我这个的价钱吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gàosu wǒ zhège de jiàqian ma?
examples.english: Can you tell me the price of this?

examples.hanzi: 菜市场的价钱比超市便宜。
examples.pinyin: Càishìchǎng de jiàqian bǐ chāoshì piányi.
examples.english: Prices at the vegetable market are cheaper than at the supermarket.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
君 (jūn) hints at the sound: 群 qún is close, as in 裙 qún.
羊 (sheep) — sheep gather in flocks, hence group; the radical also appears in 美 beautiful, 善 good.

example.hanzi: 广场上聚集了大量人群。
example.pinyin: guǎngchǎng shàng jùjí le dàliàng rénqún.
example.english: A large crowd gathered in the square.
example.fact: The Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca draws roughly two million people to a single site within the same few days each year, making crowd-flow engineering — controlling how a human crowd moves without triggering a crush — a serious scientific discipline. Saudi authorities now use real-time sensor data and one-way pedestrian corridors to manage the density.

examples.hanzi: 下班时地铁站里全是人群。
examples.pinyin: Xiàbān shí dìtiězhàn lǐ quán shì rénqún.
examples.english: The subway station is full of crowds at rush hour.

examples.hanzi: 他挤出人群，向我走来。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐ chū rénqún, xiàng wǒ zǒu lái.
examples.english: He pushed out of the crowd and walked toward me.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.

example.hanzi: 他的精神状态很好。
example.pinyin: Tā de jīngshén zhuàngtài hěn hǎo.
example.english: His mental state is very good.
example.fact: 精 began as 'polished rice' and grew to mean 'refined, essence, skilful': 精彩 (wonderful), 精神 (spirit), 精通 (be proficient in), 精确 (precise). 精 can also mean a spirit, as in 妖精.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的东西都很精美。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi dōu hěn jīngměi.
examples.english: The items in this shop are all exquisite.

examples.hanzi: 他对中国历史很精通。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ hěn jīngtōng.
examples.english: He is very knowledgeable about Chinese history.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks walls and slopes, as in 院, 阶, 附; 隔 is to separate with a partition.
鬲 (gé) gives the sound exactly: 隔 gé.

example.hanzi: 我住在你家隔壁。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài nǐ jiā gébì.
example.english: I live next door to you.
example.fact: 隔 describes an interval or barrier: 隔壁 (next door), 隔夜 (overnight) and 隔音 (soundproof). With time words it means 'every other': 隔一天 is every second day, and 隔了很久 is 'after a long gap'.

examples.hanzi: 每隔两天,我就去一次健身房。
examples.pinyin: Měi gé liǎng tiān, wǒ jiù qù yí cì jiànshēnfáng.
examples.english: I go to the gym every other day.

examples.hanzi: 一条河隔开了两个村子。
examples.pinyin: Yì tiáo hé gé kāi le liǎng ge cūnzi.
examples.english: A river separates the two villages.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 太阳能是这艘船的动力来源。
example.pinyin: tàiyángnéng shì zhè sōu chuán de dònglì láiyuán.
example.english: Solar energy is this ship's power source.
example.fact: James Watt's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, converted burning coal into reliable mechanical motive power for the first time at scale, and is widely credited with kicking off the Industrial Revolution. Before Watt, most factories still relied on water wheels or animal and human muscle for power.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车的动力很强。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē de dònglì hěn qiáng.
examples.english: This car has strong power.

examples.hanzi: 家人的支持是我努力学习的动力。
examples.pinyin: Jiārén de zhīchí shì wǒ nǔlì xuéxí de dònglì.
examples.english: My family's support is my motivation to study hard.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.

example.hanzi: 托尼喜欢弹吉他。
example.pinyin: Tuōní xǐhuan tán jítā.
example.english: Tony likes playing guitar.
example.fact: Broadway's annual Tony Awards are named after Antoinette 'Tony' Perry, a director and co-founder of the American Theatre Wing who died in 1946 just before the first ceremony was held in her honor. The trophy itself is a medallion, not a statuette, making it one of the few major entertainment awards without a human-figure trophy.

examples.hanzi: 托尼是我的同事，他很幽默。
examples.pinyin: Tuōní shì wǒ de tóngshì, tā hěn yōumò.
examples.english: Tony is my colleague, and he's very humorous.

examples.hanzi: 托尼明天要去北京出差。
examples.pinyin: Tuōní míngtiān yào qù Běijīng chūchāi.
examples.english: Tony is going to Beijing on a business trip tomorrow.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) with 月 — the shady side of a hill, the opposite of 阳 (阝 with 日, sunny); yīn is the dark principle.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — planning is done by talking things through; also 议 discuss, 论 discuss.
某 (mǒu) is a near sound match for móu; same part in 媒 méi and 煤 méi.

example.hanzi: 警方揭露了一个阴谋。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng jiēlù le yī gè yīnmóu.
example.english: The police uncovered a conspiracy.
example.fact: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605, in which Guy Fawkes and a group of conspirators tried to blow up England's Houses of Parliament and kill King James I, was foiled at the last minute after an anonymous tip. Britain still commemorates its failure every November 5th with bonfires and fireworks on Guy Fawkes Night.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里有一个大阴谋。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ yǒu yí ge dà yīnmóu.
examples.english: There is a big conspiracy in this story.

examples.hanzi: 他发现有人在策划阴谋。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāxiàn yǒu rén zài cèhuà yīnmóu.
examples.english: He discovered that someone was plotting a scheme.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 别着急,慢慢来。
example.pinyin: bié zháojí, mànmànlái.
example.english: Don't rush, take your time.
example.fact: The Slow Food movement was founded in Italy in 1986 by activist Carlo Petrini, in direct protest of a McDonald's opening near Rome's Spanish Steps. It now has chapters in over 160 countries promoting the idea that meals, and by extension life, are better savored unhurried.

examples.hanzi: 我们不用急，慢慢来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen búyòng jí, mànmàn lái.
examples.english: We don't need to rush; take it slowly.

examples.hanzi: 学语言要慢慢来，不能太急。
examples.pinyin: Xué yǔyán yào mànmàn lái, bù néng tài jí.
examples.english: Learning a language takes time and can't be rushed.

components.note: 良 (liáng) — good; as a part it sounds out 粮 liáng, 狼 láng, 浪 làng and 朗 lǎng.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 他的考试成绩良好。
example.pinyin: tā de kǎoshì chéngjì liánghǎo.
example.english: His exam results are good.
example.fact: HDL cholesterol is often nicknamed 'good' cholesterol because it scavenges excess cholesterol from artery walls and carries it back to the liver for disposal, rather than depositing it as plaque. Regular aerobic exercise is one of the few reliably proven ways to raise a person's HDL levels.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的服务非常良好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de fúwù fēicháng liánghǎo.
examples.english: The service at this hotel is very good.

examples.hanzi: 良好的习惯会让你受益一生。
examples.pinyin: Liánghǎo de xíguàn huì ràng nǐ shòuyì yìshēng.
examples.english: Good habits will benefit you for life.

components.note: 尸 (body) — the top part: a person. Dictionary: a man measuring by pacing; with the stroke below it, the stride or a ruler.
乚 (hook) — the bottom stroke, the measuring step. Memory aid: a foot-length ruler, as in 英尺 foot (unit).

example.hanzi: 请把尺子借给我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chǐzi jiè gěi wǒ.
example.english: Please lend me the ruler.
example.fact: In the traditional measure, 1 尺 (市尺) is one third of a metre, so 三尺 is about a metre. It forms 尺子 (a ruler), 尺寸 (size, dimensions) and 卷尺 (tape measure); in music, 尺 is also a note name.

examples.hanzi: 这块红布有三尺长。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài hóngbù yǒu sān chǐ cháng.
examples.english: This piece of red cloth is three chi long.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用卷尺量一量。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng juǎnchǐ liáng yi liáng.
examples.english: You can measure it with a tape measure.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 医生救了他的性命。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiù le tā de xìngmìng.
example.english: The doctor saved his life.
example.fact: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs), now common in airports, offices, and stadiums, can more than double a cardiac-arrest victim's chance of survival when used within the first few minutes of collapse. Every minute of delay before defibrillation lowers survival odds by roughly 7 to 10 percent.

examples.hanzi: 他为了救孩子，冒着性命危险。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile jiù háizi, màozhe xìngmìng wēixiǎn.
examples.english: To save the child, he risked his life.

examples.hanzi: 他们不顾性命地跑进火场。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen búgù xìngmìng de pǎo jìn huǒchǎng.
examples.english: They ran into the fire at the risk of their lives.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".

example.hanzi: 为此,政府决定采取新措施。
example.pinyin: wèi cǐ, zhèngfǔ juédìng cǎiqǔ xīn cuòshī.
example.english: For this reason, the government decided to adopt new measures.
example.fact: In 1961, East Germany began construction of the Berlin Wall overnight, citing the need to stop the mass emigration of skilled workers to the West — for that stated reason, families on both sides woke up to find their city physically divided. The wall stood for 28 years before falling in 1989.

examples.hanzi: 为此，我特意请了一天假。
examples.pinyin: Wèicǐ, wǒ tèyì qǐng le yì tiān jià.
examples.english: For this reason, I took a day off on purpose.

examples.hanzi: 我们为此准备了很久。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wèicǐ zhǔnbèi le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: We've been preparing for this for a long time.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wood radical — tables are wooden furniture, like 椅 chair, 板 board.
卓 (zhuō) — same sound as 桌 zhuō — a clear sound clue.

example.hanzi: 书放在桌子上。
example.pinyin: Shū fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: The book is on the table.
example.fact: 桌 appears mostly in 桌子 (table) and 书桌 (desk). It is also the measure word for dinner tables: 一桌菜 means 'a table full of dishes', and 开了十桌 'ten tables were set up for the banquet'.

examples.hanzi: 请把碗筷摆在桌上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wǎnkuài bǎi zài zhuō shang.
examples.english: Please put the bowls and chopsticks on the table.

examples.hanzi: 晚饭已经摆上餐桌了。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnfàn yǐjīng bǎi shàng cānzhuō le.
examples.english: Dinner is already on the table.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.hanzi: 农民用稻草人赶走鸟儿。
example.pinyin: nóngmín yòng dàocǎorén gǎnzǒu niǎor.
example.english: The farmer used a scarecrow to drive away the birds.
example.fact: Scarecrows have been used to drive birds off farmland for over 3,000 years, with early versions recorded in ancient Egypt, where farmers stood in fields waving cloth to protect wheat from flocks of quail. Modern farms have largely replaced them with propane cannons and predator-shaped drones.

examples.hanzi: 他把小狗从院子里赶走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiǎo gǒu cóng yuànzi lǐ gǎnzǒu le.
examples.english: He drove the puppy out of the yard.

examples.hanzi: 我们得把蚊子赶走。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děi bǎ wénzi gǎnzǒu.
examples.english: We have to chase the mosquitoes away.

components.note: 二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.
十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.

example.hanzi: 她今年二十岁了。
example.pinyin: tā jīnnián èrshí suì le.
example.english: She is twenty years old this year.
example.fact: The ancient Maya civilization built its entire mathematical and calendar system on a base-20 (vigesimal) counting scheme rather than the base-10 system most of the world uses today. Many scholars trace base-20 counting systems, found from Mesoamerica to West Africa, to the simple habit of counting on both fingers and toes.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟二十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi èrshí suì le.
examples.english: My younger brother is twenty years old.

examples.hanzi: 这个包二十块钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo èrshí kuài qián.
examples.english: This bag costs twenty yuan.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.

example.hanzi: 警察腰间佩戴着一支手枪。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá yāojiān pèidài zhe yī zhī shǒuqiāng.
example.english: The police officer wears a pistol at his waist.
example.fact: Samuel Colt patented the first commercially successful revolving-cylinder pistol in 1836, allowing a shooter to fire multiple rounds without reloading between each shot. Mass production techniques Colt pioneered for the revolver later influenced how many other industrial goods came to be manufactured with interchangeable parts.

examples.hanzi: 他从抽屉里拿出一支玩具手枪。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng chōutì lǐ ná chū yì zhī wánjù shǒuqiāng.
examples.english: He took a toy pistol out of the drawer.

examples.hanzi: 警察收缴了他的手枪。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá shōujiǎo le tā de shǒuqiāng.
examples.english: The police confiscated his pistol.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 工厂里有几百名工人。
example.pinyin: gōngchǎng lǐ yǒu jǐ bǎi míng gōngrén.
example.english: There are several hundred workers in the factory.
example.fact: The Empire State Building was erected by a workforce of about 3,400 construction workers who completed the 102-story skyscraper in just 410 days during 1930 and 1931, a pace still considered remarkable by modern standards. At the project's peak, workers were placing steel at a rate of more than four floors per week.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸是一名工人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba shì yì míng gōngrén.
examples.english: My dad is a worker.

examples.hanzi: 工人们正在修马路。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài xiū mǎlù.
examples.english: The workers are repairing the road.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.hanzi: 他自愿去帮助灾区的人们。
example.pinyin: tā zìyuàn qù bāngzhù zāiqū de rénmen.
example.english: He volunteered to help people in the disaster area.
example.fact: The U.S. Peace Corps was founded in 1961 by President John F. Kennedy to send volunteers abroad on unpaid or low-paid service assignments. More than 240,000 Americans have since served voluntarily in over 140 countries, working on projects from education to public health.

examples.hanzi: 她自愿加入了志愿者队伍。
examples.pinyin: Tā zìyuàn jiārù le zhìyuànzhě duìwu.
examples.english: She voluntarily joined the volunteer team.

examples.hanzi: 这是自愿的，你不想参加也可以。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zìyuàn de, nǐ bù xiǎng cānjiā yě kěyǐ.
examples.english: This is voluntary; you don't have to join if you don't want to.

components.note: 子 (child) — 子 means child, as in 孩, 孙; 孤 is a lone child, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) — near sound — 孤 is gū; 瓜 also sounds out 狐 hú and 弧 hú.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 一个人在家,他感到很孤单。
example.pinyin: yī gè rén zài jiā, tā gǎndào hěn gūdān.
example.english: Alone at home, he feels very lonely.
example.fact: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, launched in 1977, is now more than 24 billion kilometers from Earth, making it the most physically isolated object ever built by humans. It takes over 22 hours for a radio signal to travel one way between Voyager 1 and mission control.

examples.hanzi: 刚搬到新城市，她觉得很孤单。
examples.pinyin: Gāng bān dào xīn chéngshì, tā juéde hěn gūdān.
examples.english: Having just moved to a new city, she felt lonely.

examples.hanzi: 老人一个人生活，很孤单。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén yí ge rén shēnghuó, hěn gūdān.
examples.english: The old man lives alone and is lonely.

components.note: 十 (ten, many) — traditional 協 pairs 十 with three 力 (strength) side by side: many forces joined in effort, so cooperation.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 她加入了当地的音乐协会。
example.pinyin: tā jiārù le dàngdì de yīnyuè xiéhuì.
example.english: She joined the local music association.
example.fact: The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in 1863 by Swiss businessman Henri Dunant after he witnessed the aftermath of the Battle of Solferino, where thousands of wounded soldiers went without care. Dunant's advocacy led directly to the first Geneva Convention the following year and, in 1901, the first Nobel Peace Prize.

examples.hanzi: 这个协会每年举办一次比赛。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiéhuì měi nián jǔbàn yí cì bǐsài.
examples.english: This association holds a competition every year.

examples.hanzi: 他是摄影协会的会员。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì shèyǐng xiéhuì de huìyuán.
examples.english: He is a member of the photography association.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 棵 is the measure word for trees.
果 (guǒ) — close sound: 棵 kē. 果 also sounds out 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 院子里有一棵大树。
example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yì kē dà shù.
example.english: There is a big tree in the yard.
example.fact: 棵 is the measure word for whole plants and trees — 一棵树, 一棵白菜 (a head of cabbage), 一棵草. Flowers use 朵, and leaves use 片, so don't use 棵 for those.

examples.hanzi: 路边种了几棵小树。
examples.pinyin: Lù biān zhòng le jǐ kē xiǎoshù.
examples.english: A few small trees were planted by the roadside.

examples.hanzi: 他从菜地里拔了一棵白菜。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng càidì li bá le yì kē báicài.
examples.english: He pulled a Chinese cabbage from the vegetable plot.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and throat, as in 吃, 咽, 喝; 喉 is the throat.
侯 (hóu) gives the sound exactly: 喉 hóu, also in 猴 hóu.
口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and throat, as in 吃, 咽, 喝; 咙 is the throat (喉咙).
龙 (lóng) gives the sound exactly: 咙 lóng, also in 聋 lóng and 笼 lóng.

example.hanzi: 他喉咙痛,说不出话来。
example.pinyin: tā hóulóng tòng, shuō bu chū huà lái.
example.english: His throat hurts, he can't speak.
example.fact: Humans are among the few mammals whose larynx sits lower in the throat than in other primates, creating a longer vocal tract that allows the wide range of distinct vowel sounds needed for spoken language. This lower larynx position, however, is also why humans are more prone to choking than most other animals.

examples.hanzi: 我的喉咙有点干，想喝水。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de hóulóng yǒudiǎn gān, xiǎng hē shuǐ.
examples.english: My throat is a bit dry and I want to drink water.

examples.hanzi: 医生看了看我的喉咙。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng kàn le kàn wǒ de hóulóng.
examples.english: The doctor took a look at my throat.

components.note: 足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在公园里踢足球。
example.pinyin: háizimen zài gōngyuán lǐ tī zúqiú.
example.english: The kids are playing soccer in the park.
example.fact: One of the earliest known ball games resembling soccer, called cuju, was played in China during the Han dynasty over 2,000 years ago and involved kicking a leather ball through a hoop without using the hands. FIFA has officially recognized cuju as the earliest form of the sport with documented evidence.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸喜欢看足球比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba xǐhuan kàn zúqiú bǐsài.
examples.english: My dad likes watching soccer matches.

examples.hanzi: 他买了一个新足球。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yí ge xīn zúqiú.
examples.english: He bought a new soccer ball.

meanings: to see with one's own eyes

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 一位目击者描述了事故的经过。
example.pinyin: yī wèi mùjīzhě miáoshù le shìgù de jīngguò.
example.english: A witness described how the accident happened.
example.fact: Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's research beginning in the 1970s showed that eyewitness memory is far less reliable than juries tend to assume — leading questions alone could implant false details into a witness's recollection of an event they genuinely saw. Her work has since contributed to the exoneration of numerous wrongly convicted people whose cases relied heavily on eyewitness testimony.

examples.hanzi: 有一位目击者看到了小偷逃跑。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu yí wèi mùjīzhě kàn dào le xiǎotōu táopǎo.
examples.english: An eyewitness saw the thief run away.

examples.hanzi: 很多人目击了这次事故。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén mùjī le zhè cì shìgù.
examples.english: Many people witnessed this accident.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 炸, 热; 爆 is to burst in flames.
暴 (bào) sounds exactly like 爆, and means violent.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 火山突然爆发了。
example.pinyin: huǒshān tūrán bàofā le.
example.english: The volcano suddenly erupted.
example.fact: Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD, burying the Roman city of Pompeii under several meters of ash and pumice within about 24 hours, preserving buildings, artifacts, and even the forms of victims caught in the disaster. The eruption released roughly 100,000 times the thermal energy of the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima.

examples.hanzi: 两个人突然爆发了争吵。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge rén tūrán bàofā le zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: The two people suddenly burst into an argument.

examples.hanzi: 战争在一九一四年爆发。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng zài yī jiǔ yī sì nián bàofā.
examples.english: The war broke out in 1914.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 礼, 福, 祈; 祝 is to wish.
兄 (older brother) — an opened mouth before the altar: the one who speaks the prayer or blessing.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.

example.hanzi: 朋友们送上了真诚的祝福。
example.pinyin: péngyoumen sòngshàng le zhēnchéng de zhùfú.
example.english: Friends offered sincere blessings.
example.fact: The custom of saying 'bless you' after a sneeze is often traced to the Bubonic Plague era in medieval Europe, when a sneeze was taken as an early symptom of the disease and a blessing was offered in hope of warding off death. Similar sneeze-related blessing customs, however, appear even earlier in ancient Roman and Greek writings.

examples.hanzi: 新年到了，祝福你和家人健康快乐。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián dào le, zhùfú nǐ hé jiārén jiànkāng kuàilè.
examples.english: The new year is here; I wish you and your family health and happiness.

examples.hanzi: 大家都祝福这对新人幸福。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zhùfú zhè duì xīnrén xìngfú.
examples.english: Everyone wishes the newlyweds happiness.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 他证明了自己的清白。
example.pinyin: tā zhèngmíng le zìjǐ de qīngbái.
example.english: He proved his innocence.
example.fact: The presumption of innocence — the principle that an accused person is treated as innocent until proven guilty — traces back to Roman law, summarized in the maxim 'Ei incumbit probatio qui dicit, non qui negat' ('the burden of proof lies with who declares, not who denies'). The principle was later written explicitly into the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

examples.hanzi: 法院证明他是清白的。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn zhèngmíng tā shì qīngbái de.
examples.english: The court proved that he is innocent.

examples.hanzi: 她想保持名声清白。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎochí míngshēng qīngbái.
examples.english: She wants to keep her reputation spotless.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
两 (liǎng) — two, a pair; as a part it sounds out 辆 liàng and 俩 liǎ.

example.hanzi: 请给我一两个苹果就好。
example.pinyin: qǐng gěi wǒ yī liǎng gè píngguǒ jiù hǎo.
example.english: Please just give me one or two apples.
example.fact: The liang, a traditional Chinese unit of weight once used to measure silver currency, was standardized at roughly 37.3 grams under the Qing dynasty and is fixed today at exactly 50 grams. For centuries, merchants carried scales specifically to weigh out silver ingots by the liang for large transactions, long before paper currency became standard.

examples.hanzi: 我只需要一两天就能做完。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ xūyào yì liǎng tiān jiù néng zuò wán.
examples.english: I only need a day or two to finish.

examples.hanzi: 他来过一两次，但是不太熟。
examples.pinyin: Tā lái guo yì liǎng cì, dànshì bú tài shú.
examples.english: He's come once or twice, but isn't very familiar.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拿, 提; 措 is to handle or arrange.
昔 (xī) is a loose hint for cuò; 错 cuò shares it.
方 (square; flag) — stands in for the flag part 㫃 of the old form, as in 旗 flag, 旅 travel, 族 clan; the meaning 'bestow, carry out' came later.
㐌 (looks like 也 plus a stroke) — traditionally the sound part (也 yě); today the match with shī is only a loose clue.

example.hanzi: 政府采取了紧急措施应对疫情。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ le jǐnjí cuòshī yìngduì yìqíng.
example.english: The government took emergency measures to respond to the epidemic.
example.fact: The English word 'quarantine' comes from the Venetian practice, starting around 1377, of isolating ships from plague-affected ports for 'quaranta giorni' — forty days — before allowing anyone ashore. It remains one of the earliest recorded public-health measures still recognizably in use today.

examples.hanzi: 学校采取了很多安全措施。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào cǎiqǔ le hěn duō ānquán cuòshī.
examples.english: The school has taken many safety measures.

examples.hanzi: 我们得想出新的措施。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děi xiǎng chū xīn de cuòshī.
examples.english: We need to come up with new measures.

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.

example.hanzi: 两个孩子在争玩具。
example.pinyin: Liǎng gè háizi zài zhēng wánjù.
example.english: The two children are fighting over a toy.
example.fact: 争 means to contend for something, so it fits 争取 (strive for), 争论 (debate) and 争吵 (quarrel). 争 is the simplified form of 爭, which shows two hands pulling a thing in opposite directions.

examples.hanzi: 他们在为一件小事争吵。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài wèi yí jiàn xiǎoshì zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: They are arguing over a small matter.

examples.hanzi: 大家都想争第一名。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu xiǎng zhēng dì-yī míng.
examples.english: Everyone wants to compete for first place.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree 木 boxed in by an enclosure 囗: trapped, hemmed in; hence 困难 difficulty.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 扰 is to stir up and disturb.
尤 (yóu) is only a loose sound hint for rǎo.

example.hanzi: 这个问题一直困扰着科学家。
example.pinyin: zhège wèntí yī zhí kùnrǎo zhe kēxuéjiā.
example.english: This problem has long perplexed scientists.
example.fact: The trolley problem, a thought experiment first formalized by philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967, asks whether it is right to divert a runaway trolley to kill one person instead of five — a dilemma that has perplexed ethicists for decades and now shapes real debates over how self-driving cars should be programmed to react in unavoidable-crash scenarios.

examples.hanzi: 噪音让邻居们很困扰。
examples.pinyin: Zàoyīn ràng línjūmen hěn kùnrǎo.
examples.english: The noise is troubling the neighbors.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题长期困扰着他。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí chángqī kùnrǎo zhe tā.
examples.english: This problem has troubled him for a long time.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陷 is falling into a pit.
臽 (xiàn) — same sound — 陷 is xiàn; 臽 also sounds out 馅 xiàn.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 他被同事陷害,失去了工作。
example.pinyin: tā bèi tóngshì xiànhài, shīqù le gōngzuò.
example.english: He was framed by a colleague and lost his job.
example.fact: The Dreyfus Affair, which began in France in 1894, saw army officer Alfred Dreyfus wrongly convicted of treason based on forged documents, largely because he was Jewish. The case split French society for over a decade before Dreyfus was fully exonerated in 1906, and it remains one of history's most studied examples of a person framed on fabricated evidence.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的坏人想陷害主角。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàirén xiǎng xiànhài zhǔjué.
examples.english: The villain in the movie wants to frame the hero.

examples.hanzi: 他觉得自己被人陷害了。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ bèi rén xiànhài le.
examples.english: He feels that he was set up by someone.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 我们需要进一步调查这个问题。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xūyào jìn yī bù diàochá zhège wèntí.
example.english: We need to investigate this issue further.
example.fact: When Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon in July 1969, he described it as 'one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind' — a single further step that, in scientific terms, opened the door to decades of subsequent lunar and planetary exploration.

examples.hanzi: 我们要进一步了解客户的需求。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào jìnyíbù liǎojiě kèhù de xūqiú.
examples.english: We need to learn more about the customers' needs.

examples.hanzi: 双方的关系进一步改善了。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng de guānxi jìnyíbù gǎishàn le.
examples.english: The relationship between the two sides improved further.

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks eyes and seeing, as in 看, 眼, 睡; 瞄 is to aim.
苗 (miáo) gives the sound exactly: 瞄 miáo, also in 描 miáo.
冫 (ice) — cold, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 冻 freeze; here it stands for 氵 water in 準 (a water level, so exact).
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) gives only a loose sound clue for zhǔn.

example.hanzi: 猎人瞄准了远处的目标。
example.pinyin: lièrén miáozhǔn le yuǎnchù de mùbiāo.
example.english: The hunter aimed at the distant target.
example.fact: The Hubble Space Telescope can lock onto and hold a distant target with such precision that, translated to an earthbound analogy, it is roughly equivalent to holding a laser pointer steady on a coin from over 300 kilometers away. That stability, maintained by gyroscopes and guide-star tracking, is what allows Hubble to take multi-hour exposures of extremely faint galaxies.

examples.hanzi: 射手慢慢瞄准了靶心。
examples.pinyin: Shèshǒu mànman miáozhǔn le báxīn.
examples.english: The archer slowly aimed at the bullseye.

examples.hanzi: 你先瞄准再扔。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān miáozhǔn zài rēng.
examples.english: Aim first, then throw.

components.note: 化 (change) — one person 亻 beside an upside-down person 匕 — a change of state; 化 is to change, as in 文化 and 变化.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 她在大学里学习化学。
example.pinyin: tā zài dàxué lǐ xuéxí huàxué.
example.english: She studies chemistry at university.
example.fact: Marie Curie remains the only person in history to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — Physics in 1903 for her work on radioactivity, and Chemistry in 1911 for isolating the elements polonium and radium. Her original research notebooks are still radioactive today and are stored in lead-lined boxes at the French national library.

examples.hanzi: 化学课上我们做了一个实验。
examples.pinyin: Huàxué kè shàng wǒmen zuò le yí ge shíyàn.
examples.english: In chemistry class we did an experiment.

examples.hanzi: 这种化学产品对皮肤不好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng huàxué chǎnpǐn duì pífū bù hǎo.
examples.english: This chemical product is not good for the skin.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 胡 first meant the flesh hanging under the chin.
古 (gǔ) — near sound — 胡 is hú; 古 also sounds out 湖 hú and 糊 hú.

example.hanzi: 你别胡说，这不是真的。
example.pinyin: Nǐ bié húshuō, zhè bú shì zhēn de.
example.english: Don't talk nonsense; it isn't true.
example.fact: 胡 once labelled non-Han peoples to the north and west, which is why imported things carry it: 胡椒 (pepper), 胡萝卜 (carrot), 胡桃 (walnut). On its own it means 'recklessly': 胡说 (talk nonsense), 胡闹 (act up).

examples.hanzi: 他留着一把大胡子。
examples.pinyin: Tā liú zhe yì bǎ dà húzi.
examples.english: He has a big beard.

examples.hanzi: 别胡思乱想了。
examples.pinyin: Bié húsīluànxiǎng le.
examples.english: Stop letting your imagination run wild.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth, owe) — marks wanting and owing, as in 歌, 欢, 欲; 款 is a sum owed or paid.

example.hanzi: 这款手机很受欢迎。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī hěn shòu huānyíng.
example.english: This model of phone is very popular.
example.fact: 款 has two daily uses: money (付款 pay, 存款 deposit, 贷款 loan) and 'style/model' as a measure word: 一款手机 'a phone model', 新款 'new style'. It also counts clauses in a contract or law.

examples.hanzi: 这款裙子有三种颜色。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn qúnzi yǒu sān zhǒng yánsè.
examples.english: This style of dress comes in three colors.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用手机付款。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī fùkuǎn.
examples.english: You can pay with your phone.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 is grass and plants, as in 草, 花, 菜; 荒 is land overgrown with weeds, wasteland.
亡 (wáng) — loose hint — 荒 is huāng; 亡 also sounds out 慌 huāng, 谎 huǎng and 忙 máng.
唐 (táng) — the Tang dynasty; as a part it sounds out 糖 táng and 塘 táng.

example.hanzi: 这个借口听起来很荒唐。
example.pinyin: zhège jièkǒu tīng qǐlái hěn huāngtáng.
example.english: This excuse sounds absurd.
example.fact: Samuel Beckett's 1953 play 'Waiting for Godot,' in which two characters wait endlessly for someone who never arrives, became the defining work of what critics later called the Theatre of the Absurd. The movement deliberately embraced illogical, seemingly pointless situations to reflect a post-war sense that life itself often lacks clear meaning.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事太荒唐了，谁也不信。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi tài huāngtáng le, shéi yě bú xìn.
examples.english: This story is so absurd that nobody believes it.

examples.hanzi: 他做了一件荒唐的事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò le yí jiàn huāngtáng de shì.
examples.english: He did something ridiculous.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢.
周 (zhōu) is a loose sound clue for diào/tiáo; 周 also in 凋 diāo.
正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.

example.hanzi: 请调整一下椅子的高度。
example.pinyin: qǐng tiáozhěng yī xià yǐzi de gāodù.
example.english: Please adjust the height of the chair.
example.fact: The human eye's pupil can adjust its diameter roughly fourfold within a fraction of a second, automatically dilating in dim light to let in more light and constricting in bright light to protect the retina. This reflex, called the pupillary light reflex, is one of the fastest involuntary adjustments the human body makes.

examples.hanzi: 天气变冷了，我们需要调整计划。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn lěng le, wǒmen xūyào tiáozhěng jìhuà.
examples.english: The weather has turned cold, so we need to adjust the plan.

examples.hanzi: 她正在调整自己的心情。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài tiáozhěng zìjǐ de xīnqíng.
examples.english: She is adjusting her mood.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and news, as in 说, 话, 讲; 讯 is a message or an inquiry.
卂 (xùn) gives the sound exactly: 讯 xùn, also in 迅 xùn.

example.hanzi: 警察对嫌疑人进行了审讯。
example.pinyin: jǐngchá duì xiányírén jìnxíng le shěnxùn.
example.english: The police interrogated the suspect.
example.fact: The 1966 U.S. Supreme Court case Miranda v. Arizona established that police must inform suspects of their right to remain silent and to an attorney before an interrogation, after Ernesto Miranda's confession was thrown out for having been obtained without that warning. The resulting 'Miranda rights' warning is now standard procedure across American law enforcement.

examples.hanzi: 审讯持续了整整一夜。
examples.pinyin: Shěnxùn chíxù le zhěngzhěng yí yè.
examples.english: The interrogation lasted a whole night.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在审讯嫌疑人。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài shěnxùn xiányírén.
examples.english: The police are interrogating the suspect.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 大家可以随意选择座位。
example.pinyin: dàjiā kěyǐ suíyì xuǎnzé zuòwèi.
example.english: Everyone can choose their seat as they wish.
example.fact: In jazz improvisation, musicians often play freely over a chord structure without a fixed written score, inventing melodies in real time in response to what the other players are doing. This tradition of structured spontaneity, refined by figures like Charlie Parker and Miles Davis in the mid-20th century, remains a defining feature of the genre.

examples.hanzi: 你可以随意坐，别客气。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ suíyì zuò, bié kèqi.
examples.english: Sit wherever you like; make yourself at home.

examples.hanzi: 别随意丢垃圾。
examples.pinyin: Bié suíyì diū lājī.
examples.english: Don't litter carelessly.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.

example.hanzi: 他是这个职位的最佳人选。
example.pinyin: tā shì zhège zhíwèi de zuìjiā rénxuǎn.
example.english: He is the best candidate for this position.
example.fact: When choosing a new pope, the Catholic Church's College of Cardinals is sequestered inside the Sistine Chapel for a papal conclave, cut off from outside communication until a candidate receives a two-thirds majority vote. The famous colored smoke — black for no decision, white for a chosen candidate — has signaled the outcome to crowds in St. Peter's Square since the 1800s.

examples.hanzi: 我们还在找合适的人选。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hái zài zhǎo héshì de rénxuǎn.
examples.english: We are still looking for a suitable candidate.

examples.hanzi: 他是班长的最佳人选。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bānzhǎng de zuìjiā rénxuǎn.
examples.english: He is the best choice for class monitor.

meanings: junior ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: 小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.
木 (tree) — wood and trees, as in 树, 林, 桌: 校 first meant a wooden frame or restraint.
交 (jiāo) is a close sound clue for xiào; 交 also in 较 jiào and 校 xiào.

example.hanzi: 他去年被提升为少校。
example.pinyin: tā qùnián bèi tíshēng wéi shàoxiào.
example.english: He was promoted to major last year.
example.fact: The military rank of major dates back to 16th-century Spanish and French armies, where it originally referred to the officer responsible for coordinating a regiment's supplies and administration rather than commanding troops in battle. Under NATO's standardized rank codes, major corresponds to OF-3, sitting between captain and lieutenant colonel in most armed forces today.

examples.hanzi: 少校命令部队原地休息。
examples.pinyin: Shàoxiào mìnglìng bùduì yuándì xiūxi.
examples.english: The major ordered the troops to rest on the spot.

examples.hanzi: 那位少校已经退休了。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi shàoxiào yǐjīng tuìxiū le.
examples.english: That major has already retired.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.
日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; the sun over 京 gives a bright scene, hence scenery.
京 (jīng) gives the sound: 景 jǐng is close, as in 影 yǐng and 惊 jīng.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的开场场景令人印象深刻。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng de kāichǎng chǎngjǐng lìngrén yìnxiàng shēnkè.
example.english: The opening scene of this movie is impressive.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers' 1895 short film 'Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat Station' is often cited as one of cinema's first true scenes, showing a train pulling into a station from a fixed camera angle. Audience members reportedly panicked and ducked in their seats, unaccustomed to seeing a life-sized moving image appear to approach them.

examples.hanzi: 这个场景我在梦里见过。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎngjǐng wǒ zài mèng lǐ jiàn guo.
examples.english: I've seen this scene in a dream.

examples.hanzi: 电影里有很多海边的场景。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ yǒu hěn duō hǎibiān de chǎngjǐng.
examples.english: There are many seaside scenes in the movie.

components.note: 飞 (fly) — simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 我的梦想是成为一名飞行员。
example.pinyin: wǒ de mèngxiǎng shì chéngwéi yī míng fēixíngyuán.
example.english: My dream is to become a pilot.
example.fact: Amelia Earhart became the first female pilot to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean in 1932, a journey of nearly 15 hours that helped launch her into worldwide fame. She disappeared five years later while attempting to circumnavigate the globe, and neither her plane nor her remains have ever been conclusively found.

examples.hanzi: 飞行员正在检查飞机。
examples.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán zhèngzài jiǎnchá fēijī.
examples.english: The pilot is checking the plane.

examples.hanzi: 我叔叔是一名飞行员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shūshu shì yì míng fēixíngyuán.
examples.english: My uncle is a pilot.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他跑步的速度惊人。
example.pinyin: tā pǎobù de sùdù jīngrén.
example.english: His running speed is astonishing.
example.fact: A cheetah can accelerate from a standstill to 100 kilometers per hour in about three seconds, faster than most production sports cars, though it can only sustain that top speed for roughly 20 to 30 seconds before overheating. This makes the cheetah the fastest land animal on Earth despite lacking the stamina to run down prey over long distances.

examples.hanzi: 这座塔的高度惊人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò tǎ de gāodù jīngrén.
examples.english: The height of this tower is astonishing.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子的记忆力很惊人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi de jìyìlì hěn jīngrén.
examples.english: This child's memory is amazing.
